scenes.line1: Why can't Python threads run in parallel?
scenes.say: Ever wondered why Python threads don't really run in parallel? Let's see what's changing soon.

scenes.label: GIL
scenes.sub: The Global Interpreter Lock blocks true thread parallelism in CPython.
scenes.say: The Global Interpreter Lock, or GIL, stops Python threads from running at the same time. It limits how much you can use multiple cores.
With the GIL, threads share a single core, so CPU-heavy work is slow. Free-threaded Python lets threads use all cores for real parallelism.
Here's a threading example. Right now, even with four threads, the GIL keeps them from running in parallel for CPU tasks.

scenes.question: Can threads run CPU tasks in parallel today?
scenes.wrong: Yes, Python threads use all cores.
scenes.right: No, the GIL blocks true parallelism for CPU-bound threads.
scenes.say: Interviewers love this: Can Python threads run CPU tasks in parallel today? The answer is no, because the GIL blocks it.
